title: ELO Realignment and Strategic Engagement Reform Act of 2026
official_title: To provide for the reorganization and realignment of the Engagement, Liaison, and Outreach Office of the Department of Homeland Security, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: House passage recorded July 13, 2026 per the latest action. Sponsored by a Republican member with two cosponsors; referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security. The measure now moves to the Senate.
summary: Directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to submit a comprehensive plan within 120 days for reorganizing the Engagement, Liaison, and Outreach Office (ELO) inside the Office of Intelligence and Analysis (I&A) and realigning its essential functions and personnel into the Partner Engagement directorate of I&A. The plan must identify redundant or non-essential positions, programs, or functions; establish clear communication protocols with priority law enforcement agencies; centralize points of contact; enhance information-sharing; reduce outreach duplication across DHS components; and improve accountability and performance metrics. The Secretary must certify commencement of implementation within 60 days of starting the plan, and until both the plan is submitted and implementation is certified, the Secretary may not expand ELO's staffing, budget, or programmatic scope, nor establish new offices duplicating ELO's or the Partner Engagement directorate's mission without specific congressional authorization.
brief: Requires DHS to submit within 120 days a plan to reorganize the Engagement, Liaison, and Outreach Office and fold its essential functions into I&A's Partner Engagement directorate, and freezes ELO expansion until the plan is submitted and implementation is certified.

top_lines.headline: 120-Day DHS Reorganization Plan
subs: Secretary must submit a comprehensive plan to the House Homeland Security Committee and the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee
Plan must identify redundant or non-essential ELO positions, programs, or functions
Plan must realign ELO's essential functions and personnel within I&A's Partner Engagement directorate

top_lines.headline: Coordination Requirements
subs: Establish clear communication protocols with priority law enforcement agencies
Centralize points of contact for law enforcement engagement
Reduce outreach duplication across DHS components
Improve accountability and performance metrics related to stakeholder engagement

top_lines.headline: Plan Content Requirements
subs: Detailed staffing proposals, including reassignment plans
Transition timeline for realignment within I&A's Partner Engagement directorate
Internal oversight mechanisms to monitor implementation
Assurance of continuity of intelligence support and convenings to State, local, Tribal, and territorial (SLTT) entity partners, including relevant HSIN-INTEL access

top_lines.headline: Certification and Freeze
subs: Certification of implementation commencement due within 60 days of starting the plan
Until plan is submitted and implementation is certified, Secretary may not expand ELO's staffing, budget, or programmatic scope
Secretary may not establish new offices duplicating ELO or Partner Engagement mission without specific congressional authorization

items.main: Names the Act the "ELO Realignment and Strategic Engagement Reform Act of 2026."
items.detail: Short-title section only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Plan for Reorganization and Realignment of DHS Engagement, Liaison, and Outreach Office

items.main: Not later than 120 days after enactment, the Secretary must submit to the House Homeland Security Committee and Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee a comprehensive plan to identify redundant or non-essential ELO positions, programs, or functions; realign ELO's essential functions and personnel within the Partner Engagement directorate of I&A; and improve coordination with priority law enforcement agencies.
items.detail: The coordination improvements listed in subsection (a)(3) are establishing clear communication protocols, centralizing points of contact, enhancing information-sharing, reducing outreach duplication across DHS components, and improving accountability and performance metrics.

items.main: Plan must include an organizational analysis justifying the reorganization (with cost-benefit estimates), detailed staffing proposals including reassignment plans, a transition timeline for the realignment, internal oversight mechanisms, recommendations for future engagement models, and assurance of continuity of intelligence support and convenings to SLTT entity partners, including relevant HSIN-INTEL access.
items.detail: Subsection (b) enumerates six specific plan requirements. Continuity of intelligence support to State, local, Tribal, and territorial partners is called out separately in paragraph (6).

items.main: Not later than 60 days after commencing implementation of the plan, the Secretary must submit a certification to the same congressional committees.

Until the Secretary submits the plan and certifies implementation, the Secretary may not expand ELO's staffing, budget, or programmatic scope, and may not establish new offices in DHS duplicating ELO's or the Partner Engagement directorate's mission without specific congressional authorization.
items.detail: Subsection (d) is the pre-plan expansion freeze — it applies until both the plan is submitted (subsection (a)) and implementation commencement is certified (subsection (c)).

items.main: Defines "Department" (DHS), "ELO Office" (Engagement, Liaison, and Outreach office within I&A), "I&A" (Office of Intelligence and Analysis), "Secretary" (of Homeland Security), "SLTT entity" (via section 2200 of the Homeland Security Act of 2002, 6 U.S.C. 650), and "priority law enforcement agencies" (Federal, State, and local law enforcement agencies identified by the Secretary as key partners for national security, counterterrorism, emergency response, or other mission-critical operations).

gaps: The bill does not specify the total number of ELO positions or the current ELO budget baseline that the reorganization applies to.
The bill does not describe consequences if the Secretary fails to submit the plan within the 120-day deadline.
The bill does not define what a "non-essential" position or function is beyond leaving the determination to the plan itself.
The bill does not authorize any additional funds for the reorganization or transition.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Evans
featured_quotes.text: This bill consolidates the functions of two existing Department of Homeland Security offices tasked with public safety coordination into one centralized point of contact. DHS' Office of Intelligence and Analysis, also known as I&A, is the only entity in the U.S. intelligence community responsible for delivering intelligence directly to State and local law enforcement agencies.

added: 120-day DHS plan requirement to reorganize ELO and fold its essential functions into I&A's Partner Engagement directorate
Pre-plan freeze on ELO staffing, budget, or programmatic scope expansion
Prohibition on establishing new DHS offices duplicating ELO or Partner Engagement mission without specific congressional authorization
